name: cars_civil_b
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 9 car outlines seen from above, in a 3×3 grid on a flat magenta background. Every outline is the car's true length and width on one shared scale, its corners rounded as that body is, and the thick right edge of each one is the car's nose: every car points to the right. The second image shows finished cars in the art style to match. Copy its style only, not its cars or colours.

Make one image with exactly the same 3×3 layout as the first image. Inside each outline, draw the car described for that cell below, as a top-down sprite for a 2D city game.

Shape comes first:
- Fill each outline exactly: same length, same width, same corner rounding, nose at the thick edge. The car's two long sides lie on the outline's top and bottom edges: never wider than the outline, never narrower, never shorter or longer.
- The only things allowed past the outline are the two small side mirrors, one each side just ahead of the windscreen.
- Do not draw tyres or wheels at all: the game draws them itself under the body.
- Every car has its roof on. No convertible, no open top, no visible seats or people.
- Each car is mirror-symmetric about its long centre line.
- Inside a car there is no magenta at all.

Lamps:
- Inside each outline are six small thin coloured frames, a pair of each, mirror-symmetric: two dark red frames at the rear (left) corners, one near the top corner and one near the bottom corner; and at each front (right) corner one headlamp unit, framed as a blue frame with a small amber frame touching it on the side towards the car's flank.
- Each frame is where a lamp lens is drawn, filling most of its frame, in whatever shape suits that car (round, a strip, wrapped round the corner): red tail lamp glass in the red frames; in each front unit, clear headlamp glass with a chrome reflector filling the blue frame and the amber indicator lens filling the small amber frame at its outer end.
- Put each headlamp where its blue frame is and nowhere else. A previous attempt drew the headlamps out on the corners over the amber frames and left the blue frames as plain bonnet: that is wrong.
- Every car has all six lenses. The last attempt left out the amber indicators on most cars and a tail lamp on two: each small amber frame holds its own clearly orange indicator lens, separate from the clear headlamp beside it, and both red frames hold a tail lamp.
- The last attempt also drew the microcar too narrow and the beige saloon and grey SUV too wide: each body is exactly its outline's width.
- Every lamp is switched off: dark unlit glass with one small pale glint, no glow, no light cast on the body or the ground.
- The frames themselves are guides only; do not draw their lines.

Rules for every car:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no tilt, no side panels, no ground, no shadow.
- Style: match the style image. Chunky pixel art with crisp hard-edged pixels and no blur. A dark near-black outline about 2 pixels thick. Flat colour with one highlight and one shadow tone. Soft light from the top-left. Glass is dark slate blue with one pale glint.
- Bonnet, roof and boot read as separate panels, divided by the windscreen and the rear window.
- No text, logos, brand badges, licence plates, numbers, people or watermark anywhere.
- Outside the cars, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No grid lines or frames.

Cars, left to right, top to bottom, body length × width (the footprint includes the mirrors):
1. 2.75 × 1.62 m (1.7× longer than wide), widely rounded corners — two-seat city microcar, mint green with a contrasting pale grey safety-cell frame, a short stubby bonnet, a big curved windscreen and one rear window, almost no boot
2. 3.40 × 1.66 m (2.0× longer than wide), tight corners — tall boxy city car, sky blue with a white roof, a very short flat bonnet, a long flat roof reaching almost to the square tail, upright rear window
3. 3.55 × 1.70 m (2.1× longer than wide), very round corners — round retro two-door small car, cream body with a white roof, a domed rounded bonnet, round shoulders all around, a folded canvas sunroof strip down the middle of the closed roof
4. 3.95 × 1.72 m (2.3× longer than wide), rounded corners — five-door family hatchback, coral red with a gloss black roof, a short sloping bonnet, a steep rear hatch window, a small roof spoiler over it
5. 4.10 × 1.62 m (2.5× longer than wide), nearly square corners — old boxy four-door saloon from the 1980s, faded beige, flat square bonnet and boot of equal length, a thin chrome strip along each side, a small square roof
6. 4.25 × 1.80 m (2.4× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — compact crossover SUV, dark graphite grey with matt black plastic trim around the edges, a tall flat bonnet, a panoramic dark glass roof panel, black roof rails
7. 4.30 × 1.75 m (2.5× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — family estate car, navy blue, a long roof running all the way to a squared-off tail with a tall rear window, two thin silver roof rails along the roof edges
8. 4.35 × 1.80 m (2.4× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — family people carrier, deep wine red, a short sloping nose into a long steep windscreen, one long smooth roof with two small sunroof panes, a sliding-door rail line along each side
9. 4.40 × 1.82 m (2.4× longer than wide), tight corners — small courier panel van, dark forest green, a short nose and windscreen, then a long windowless flat cargo roof with two raised ribs running to the square rear doors, no lettering
